purpose: Normalize reusable queues, workspaces, lifecycle projections, boards, process steps, actions, activity, and application-shell intent for Web and native renderers without moving business authority into Ten4Seven.

system: semantic pattern intent and composition grammar
state presentation vocabulary and accessible structure
selection, focus, keyboard, press, and dismissal behavior
consumer: business data, record meaning, status labels, and priority mapping
allowed transitions, validation, authorization, and entitlements
assignment, SLA, escalation, and notification policy
fetching, filtering, sorting, pagination, persistence, and sync truth
action handlers, side effects, routing, and decision authority
drag/drop legality, reorder persistence, and conflict resolution
comment, audit, history, and collaboration backends
renderer: DOM or native primitives and platform semantics
popup versus sheet, list/detail, and safe-area presentation
measurement, scrolling, focus/press feedback, and reduced-motion execution
optional windowing or gesture engines behind an approved adapter boundary

renderInputs: consumer-defined labels, descriptions, state, timestamp, actor, and metadata
consumer-defined available actions and disabled/hidden state
consumer-defined evidence, notes, criteria, and decision result
neverOwnedByTen4Seven: workflow state machine, transition legality, guards, or side effects
business status, priority, urgency, SLA, escalation, or assignment truth
permission, authorization, entitlement, or approval authority
fetching, persistence, synchronization, conflict resolution, or audit truth
comment/chat backend, notification delivery, or domain routing
businessBoundary.priorityVocabulary: No global low/normal/high/urgent enum is introduced; consumers map their domain priority to semantic presentation and text.

dnd.movementIntent: A board may emit a renderer-neutral move intent containing stable item identity and destination identity; the consumer decides legality and persistence.
dnd.nonDndAlternative: Every task-critical move has an explicit focusable action such as Move to lane, Move before, or Move after.
dnd.keyboard: Keyboard and screen-reader users never depend on drag or hover.

WorkQueue.intent: Present operational records awaiting work, with a clear next action and bounded collection controls.
useWhen: records are available for operational processing
the consumer can supply a stable next action and record context
avoidWhen: the surface is informational notification history
one record's lifecycle is the primary task

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded collection with visible filters, selection, status, and optional contextual detail beside or in a drawer.
responsive.tablet: Preserve primary identity and next-action columns; move secondary context into detail before shrinking controls below their useful measure.
responsive.mobile: Render a readable list, then list-to-detail navigation and a safe action surface; do not squeeze a desktop table into the viewport.
responsive.native: Use a native collection and list-to-detail presentation with touch-safe rows and hardware-back return.

consumerOwns: record membership, query, filter, sort, selection, and permissions
record status, priority mapping, owner, next action, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: collection anatomy, state presentation, density, selection semantics, and focus behavior
detail presentation and adaptive list/detail/action composition
rendererOwns: semantic table/list primitives, scrolling, and platform-specific detail surface
WorkQueue.decisionBoundary: Queue membership and the meaning of work remain consumer-owned; the pattern only renders supplied records and action intents.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: dense Web collection becomes native list/detail.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create domain-specific queue primitives.

Inbox.intent: Present items requiring a person's attention or review without implying that all operational records belong in an inbox.
useWhen: attention, review, or unread work is the primary organizing meaning
the consumer can explain why an item needs attention
avoidWhen: the collection is an operational backlog with no attention semantics
the surface is durable informational notification history

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded collection with visible filters, selection, status, and optional contextual detail beside or in a drawer.
responsive.tablet: Preserve primary identity and next-action columns; move secondary context into detail before shrinking controls below their useful measure.
responsive.mobile: Render a readable list, then list-to-detail navigation and a safe action surface; do not squeeze a desktop table into the viewport.
responsive.native: Use a native collection and list-to-detail presentation with touch-safe rows and hardware-back return.

consumerOwns: attention/unread truth, assignment, priority mapping, review policy, and query state
permissions, acknowledgment, dismissal, persistence, and follow-up actions
ten4sevenOwns: attention hierarchy, accessible selected/unread presentation, and adaptive collection anatomy
rendererOwns: list/table semantics, focus/press feedback, and native list/detail presentation
Inbox.decisionBoundary: The consumer defines attention and unread semantics; Ten4Seven does not infer urgency from color, age, or a numeric priority.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: use native list/detail and safe action presentation.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create ApprovalInbox, FarmInbox, or another domain primitive.

NotificationCenter.intent: Present informational notification history and delivery state, distinct from records awaiting operational work.
useWhen: the user needs informational history or delivery status
avoidWhen: the user must process operational records or make a decision

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded notification surface anchored to application navigation or an explicit page.
responsive.tablet: Keep notification identity and unread status visible while reducing secondary metadata.
responsive.mobile: Use a full-width list or sheet with explicit dismiss/read actions.
responsive.native: Use a native notification list or sheet with clear read/dismiss semantics.

consumerOwns: notification delivery, read/dismiss persistence, routing, and permission policy
ten4sevenOwns: notification grouping, status presentation, focus, and responsive surface geometry
rendererOwns: popup/sheet/list semantics and platform dismissal behavior
NotificationCenter.decisionBoundary: Informational notification history must not silently become an operational queue or an authorization channel.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: anchored Web surface may become a native list or sheet.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not use NotificationCenter as a substitute for a domain work queue.

DecisionWorkspace.intent: Present context, evidence, history, criteria, notes, and consumer-defined decision actions in one bounded task surface.
useWhen: a decision needs evidence and context in the same task flow
avoidWhen: the surface only displays status or only collects a simple field

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded master/detail or evidence/detail composition with persistent context only when the task needs comparison.
responsive.tablet: Keep the active record and next action visible while collapsing secondary context into a drawer or stacked region.
responsive.mobile: Use list to detail to action/sheet progression; return focus or navigation to the originating record after dismissal.
responsive.native: Use a native list/detail stack, scroll surface, or sheet while preserving record identity, evidence order, and action reachability.

consumerOwns: criteria, evidence truth, notes persistence, decision options, authorization, validation, and outcome
available actions, transition legality, audit record, and side effects
ten4sevenOwns: evidence hierarchy, action grouping, decision-state presentation, focus, and adaptive composition
rendererOwns: semantic regions, scroll ownership, sticky/safe-area action presentation, and native stack/sheet
DecisionWorkspace.decisionBoundary: Generic action slots may be labelled by the consumer; the library must not expose ApproveButton, RejectButton, or decision policy.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: preserve evidence order and sticky actions in a single-column native surface.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not encode approval authority or domain-specific decision names in the pattern.

QueueDetailWorkspace.intent: Connect a bounded work collection to contextual record detail without duplicating queue and detail state.
useWhen: a queue item needs inspection without losing the collection context
avoidWhen: detail is a standalone page or the collection is not task-bearing

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded master/detail or evidence/detail composition with persistent context only when the task needs comparison.
responsive.tablet: Keep the active record and next action visible while collapsing secondary context into a drawer or stacked region.
responsive.mobile: Use list to detail to action/sheet progression; return focus or navigation to the originating record after dismissal.
responsive.native: Use a native list/detail stack, scroll surface, or sheet while preserving record identity, evidence order, and action reachability.

consumerOwns: record query, selection, detail routing, data loading, permissions, and actions
ten4sevenOwns: master/detail geometry, selection semantics, focus return, and adaptive list/detail transition
rendererOwns: split-pane, drawer, list, and native navigation presentation
QueueDetailWorkspace.decisionBoundary: Selection and record routing are consumer-controlled; the workspace only coordinates presentation seams.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: desktop split/detail becomes mobile list-detail navigation.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create OrderWorkspace, FarmWorkspace, or another domain-specific shell.

MasterDetailWorkspace.intent: Coordinate a collection and a focused detail surface for comparison or inspection tasks.
useWhen: a focused record and its collection must remain related
avoidWhen: a full-page detail route is sufficient or the task needs a decision-specific evidence layout

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded master/detail or evidence/detail composition with persistent context only when the task needs comparison.
responsive.tablet: Keep the active record and next action visible while collapsing secondary context into a drawer or stacked region.
responsive.mobile: Use list to detail to action/sheet progression; return focus or navigation to the originating record after dismissal.
responsive.native: Use a native list/detail stack, scroll surface, or sheet while preserving record identity, evidence order, and action reachability.

consumerOwns: collection membership, selected record, route/history, data, permissions, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: layout coordination, responsive recomposition, selection/focus contract, and scroll ownership
rendererOwns: desktop panes, contextual drawers, and native stack/detail navigation
MasterDetailWorkspace.decisionBoundary: The workspace does not infer selection authority or mutate the record when detail is viewed.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: native uses a stack/detail route rather than compressing two panes.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Keep the workspace domain-neutral and route/permission agnostic.

LifecycleTracker.intent: Present a consumer-supplied ordered stage projection for one bounded process or record.
useWhen: one bounded lifecycle needs stage context and progress presentation
avoidWhen: the user needs a queue of many records or a state-machine editor

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded master/detail or evidence/detail composition with persistent context only when the task needs comparison.
responsive.tablet: Keep the active record and next action visible while collapsing secondary context into a drawer or stacked region.
responsive.mobile: Use list to detail to action/sheet progression; return focus or navigation to the originating record after dismissal.
responsive.native: Use a native list/detail stack, scroll surface, or sheet while preserving record identity, evidence order, and action reachability.

consumerOwns: stage meaning, transition legality, timestamps, actor, completion truth, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: ordered stage presentation, keyboard navigation, state labels, and detail adaptation
rendererOwns: ordered/list semantics, focus behavior, drawer/sheet, and native stack presentation
LifecycleTracker.decisionBoundary: MilestoneTracker is a projection and does not expose transitions, guards, or business workflow mutation.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: native presents a compact ordered stack/detail projection.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not turn lifecycle stages into a domain-specific state engine.

Wizard.intent: Present sequential task steps with explicit navigation while the consumer owns validation and completion rules.
useWhen: the task is intentionally sequential and each step has a bounded purpose
avoidWhen: stages are merely a record lifecycle or users need free navigation across a collection

responsive.desktop: Use a visible stepper with bounded content and a stable action footer.
responsive.tablet: Keep current step and next/back actions visible while reducing secondary step descriptions.
responsive.mobile: Use compact progress plus one step at a time and keyboard/assistive-technology-readable navigation.
responsive.native: Use a compact progress header and a single scroll-owned step surface with safe-area actions.

consumerOwns: step validation, completion rules, persistence, resume policy, permissions, and side effects
ten4sevenOwns: step anatomy, navigation semantics, invalid/loading presentation, and responsive action layout
rendererOwns: focus movement, scroll ownership, native keyboard avoidance, and safe-area action presentation
Wizard.decisionBoundary: Stepper navigation is not validation authority; invalid or complete states are supplied by the consumer.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: compact progress and single-step native surface.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create domain-specific wizard primitives or hide validation policy in the library.

Kanban.intent: Present generic lanes and cards for many work items with explicit non-DnD movement paths.
useWhen: many items are compared by work stage and lane context adds value
avoidWhen: one object's lifecycle is the task or a dense comparison table is more useful

responsive.desktop: Show bounded lanes with readable cards and lane-level context; horizontal scrolling is allowed only when lane count and task justify it.
responsive.tablet: Reduce simultaneous lane density or move lane selection into a bounded navigation surface before reducing card anatomy.
responsive.mobile: Use lane tabs or a lane selector plus a vertical card list; never render five squeezed lanes as the primary task surface.
responsive.native: Use a lane selector and native list/section list; movement uses explicit actions unless a separate gesture contract is approved.

consumerOwns: lanes, cards, stage meaning, WIP policy, permissions, movement legality, persistence, and conflicts
ten4sevenOwns: lane/card anatomy, selected/moving/error states, keyboard alternative, density, and adaptive lane presentation
rendererOwns: layout, scrolling, pointer/touch feedback, and any separately approved DnD engine adapter
Kanban.decisionBoundary: Move emits intent only; a board is not a transition engine and DnD is not a completion requirement.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: desktop lanes become mobile lane selection plus a vertical list.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create domain boards or expose a donor DnD API as the Ten4Seven contract.

TaskBoard.intent: A task-oriented Kanban composition with next-action and ownership emphasis, not a new board primitive.
useWhen: the card anatomy is explicitly task-oriented and the Kanban contract already fits
avoidWhen: a new task primitive would duplicate Card, List, or ActionBar

responsive.desktop: Show bounded lanes with readable cards and lane-level context; horizontal scrolling is allowed only when lane count and task justify it.
responsive.tablet: Reduce simultaneous lane density or move lane selection into a bounded navigation surface before reducing card anatomy.
responsive.mobile: Use lane tabs or a lane selector plus a vertical card list; never render five squeezed lanes as the primary task surface.
responsive.native: Use a lane selector and native list/section list; movement uses explicit actions unless a separate gesture contract is approved.

consumerOwns: task truth, assignee, priority mapping, due dates, transitions, permissions, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: variant anatomy, state styling, action reachability, keyboard movement path, and adaptive composition
rendererOwns: lane/list layout and optional approved gesture/drag implementation
TaskBoard.decisionBoundary: Task semantics are consumer-supplied; TaskBoard is a variant decision, not a task database or transition API.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: use lane selector/list on native.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not add project-specific TaskBoard variants to the primitive catalog.

Workboard.intent: Compose board, queue, summary, and detail blocks for an operational work surface without becoming a monster component.
useWhen: a product surface needs multiple bounded workflow compositions
avoidWhen: a single queue or board recipe is sufficient

responsive.desktop: Show bounded lanes with readable cards and lane-level context; horizontal scrolling is allowed only when lane count and task justify it.
responsive.tablet: Reduce simultaneous lane density or move lane selection into a bounded navigation surface before reducing card anatomy.
responsive.mobile: Use lane tabs or a lane selector plus a vertical card list; never render five squeezed lanes as the primary task surface.
responsive.native: Use a lane selector and native list/section list; movement uses explicit actions unless a separate gesture contract is approved.

consumerOwns: which business blocks appear, data, permissions, query state, action meaning, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: block composition grammar, responsive prioritization, shared tokens, and cross-block focus conventions
rendererOwns: layout, list/table, sheet/drawer, and native lane/list composition
Workboard.decisionBoundary: Workboard is a block composition and never owns a product's workflow model, routing, or persistence.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: prioritize one work surface and move secondary blocks below or into navigation on native.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not build a monolithic Workboard primitive with domain data or permission logic.

CommandPalette.intent: Compatibility alias for CommandMenu's generic search and action discovery surface.
useWhen: existing consumers use the CommandPalette name
avoidWhen: adding a second command implementation or exposing a browser-only shortcut on native

responsive.desktop: Use the canonical CommandMenu keyboard-first overlay with explicit trigger and focus return.
responsive.tablet: Use the same command surface with a touch-safe trigger and bounded result list.
responsive.mobile: Use a search/action screen or sheet; do not require Cmd/Ctrl+K.
responsive.native: Resolve to a native search/action surface or bottom sheet with hardware-back dismissal.

consumerOwns: command registry, labels, permissions, availability, search ranking, and command handlers
ten4sevenOwns: search/result anatomy, keyboard/focus behavior, dismissal, and adaptive presentation intent
rendererOwns: Web overlay versus native screen/sheet and platform keyboard/back behavior
CommandPalette.decisionBoundary: Command execution and availability are consumer-owned; CommandPalette is only the legacy alias of CommandMenu.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: Web popup becomes native search/action screen or sheet.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Use CommandMenu in new code; do not expose CommandPalette as a second canonical primitive.

QuickActions.intent: Present a bounded set of context-appropriate actions through existing action and toolbar primitives.
useWhen: a route or record has a small bounded action set
avoidWhen: actions need a full workflow workspace, a business-specific action component, or an unbounded command registry

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded master/detail or evidence/detail composition with persistent context only when the task needs comparison.
responsive.tablet: Keep the active record and next action visible while collapsing secondary context into a drawer or stacked region.
responsive.mobile: Use list to detail to action/sheet progression; return focus or navigation to the originating record after dismissal.
responsive.native: Use a native list/detail stack, scroll surface, or sheet while preserving record identity, evidence order, and action reachability.

consumerOwns: action availability, labels, ordering, permissions, handlers, and side effects
ten4sevenOwns: action grouping, disclosure, focus, keyboard path, and adaptive action placement
rendererOwns: toolbar/footer/overflow presentation and native sheet or press feedback
QuickActions.decisionBoundary: QuickActions presents action slots and never infers permission or runs a business action itself.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: action bar/footer may become native sheet or bottom action region.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create ApproveButton, FarmActions, or another domain action primitive.

ActivityFeed.intent: Present actor/action-oriented chronological activity supplied by a consumer.
useWhen: actor/action history or chronological operational events matter
avoidWhen: comments/chat, durable audit exploration, or cross-record comparison is the primary task

responsive.desktop: Use a readable ordered activity region beside or below the primary task context.
responsive.tablet: Preserve actor, action, and time before secondary metadata.
responsive.mobile: Use a single ordered feed with optional detail activation and explicit loading/empty states.
responsive.native: Use a native ordered list with accessible actor/action/time text and optional detail navigation.

consumerOwns: event order, actor, timestamp, action meaning, loading policy, and persistence
ten4sevenOwns: ordered hierarchy, state presentation, readable measure, and platform-neutral activity anatomy
rendererOwns: list semantics, scrolling, and native list/detail presentation
ActivityFeed.decisionBoundary: Activity display is not an audit store, comment backend, notification delivery system, or state machine.

ai.platformNotes: Both: native renderer uses the same activity intent as an ordered list.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Timeline remains an alias/intent name; do not create a domain-specific feed primitive.

CommentThread.intent: Deferred collaboration composition requiring an explicit authoring, moderation, mention, and persistence contract.
useWhen: a future consumer provides the complete collaboration and moderation boundary
avoidWhen: an activity feed or read-only audit stream is sufficient

responsive.desktop: Use a bounded master/detail or evidence/detail composition with persistent context only when the task needs comparison.
responsive.tablet: Keep the active record and next action visible while collapsing secondary context into a drawer or stacked region.
responsive.mobile: Use list to detail to action/sheet progression; return focus or navigation to the originating record after dismissal.
responsive.native: Use a native list/detail stack, scroll surface, or sheet while preserving record identity, evidence order, and action reachability.

consumerOwns: authors, content, moderation, mentions, threading, persistence, sync, and conflict handling
ten4sevenOwns: future generic thread anatomy after the contract is approved
rendererOwns: text input, keyboard avoidance, native list, and safe-area presentation
CommentThread.decisionBoundary: No generic comments API or chat backend is created in U09.

ai.platformNotes: Deferred for both platforms until collaboration semantics are approved.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not approximate comments with an ActivityFeed and do not add a local thread primitive.

AppShell.intent: Coordinate application navigation, header, content, and responsive utility regions without owning business routing.
useWhen: private or operational application surfaces need coordinated navigation and content geometry
avoidWhen: a public/marketing surface needs PublicShell or a flat navigation context

responsive.desktop: Use the application shell grammar with sidebar/topbar/content and a bounded route content region.
responsive.tablet: Collapse secondary navigation and preserve page header/action hierarchy.
responsive.mobile: Use mobile navigation disclosure and keep route content single-column with safe-area-aware actions.
responsive.native: Map the shell intent to native navigation, drawer, header, and stack/detail primitives.

consumerOwns: routing, navigation model, permissions, entitlements, active route, and route content
ten4sevenOwns: shell geometry, navigation semantics, page header anatomy, focus, and responsive/adaptive composition
rendererOwns: DOM/native navigation primitives, drawer/back behavior, and viewport/safe-area handling
AppShell.decisionBoundary: AppShell coordinates presentation and never becomes an application router, permission gate, or business workflow host.

ai.platformNotes: Adaptive: desktop navigation maps to native navigation/drawer/stack presentation.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Keep shell generic; consumers supply route and permission truth.

PageHeader.intent: Provide route-level title, summary, metadata, breadcrumbs, tabs, and primary action hierarchy.
useWhen: a route needs one authoritative heading and action region
avoidWhen: a nested card or block needs a local heading

responsive.desktop: Keep title, summary, metadata, and primary action in a readable route-level region.
responsive.tablet: Prioritize title and primary action before optional metadata or tabs.
responsive.mobile: Stack title and actions while preserving heading order and touch-safe controls.
responsive.native: Use the native navigation header or a top content header with the same title/action intent.

consumerOwns: title meaning, breadcrumbs, route actions, status truth, and navigation state
ten4sevenOwns: heading hierarchy, layout, action grouping, and responsive stacking
rendererOwns: DOM heading/navigation semantics or native navigation header
PageHeader.decisionBoundary: PageHeader presents route metadata and actions; it does not resolve routing or authorization.

ai.platformNotes: Same intent: native navigation header or top content header.
ai.avoidDomainNaming: Do not create route-specific header primitives.

entity-detail.note: Canonical detail scaffold; it does not turn record status into a business transition.

process-workspace.note: Existing operational recipe linked as a process composition, not a generic workflow engine.

decision-workspace.note: Existing evidence and decision composition; decision authority remains consumer-owned.

activity-audit.note: Existing activity/audit composition; persisted audit truth and filtering remain consumer-owned.

operational-kanban.note: Existing generic operational board recipe; movement is an intent seam, not library-owned persistence.

exception-queue.note: Attention-first operational recipe; it is not the definition of every inbox or notification center.

public-shell-navigation.note: Compatibility shell block; public surfaces still use PublicShell and do not inherit private navigation by default.

workflow-board-preview.note: Catalogued block composition for board preview; it does not own lane data or DnD.

exception-queue-summary.note: Summary block for attention work; a full queue remains a consumer-composed collection.

decision-workspace-evidence.note: Evidence block; it presents supplied evidence and does not authorize a decision.

activity-audit-stream.note: Activity stream composition; comments, audit persistence, and event truth remain separate.

approval-queue-summary.note: Approval-oriented summary; it does not create an ApproveButton or approval policy.

onboarding-stepper.note: Stepper composition; validation and completion rules remain consumer-owned.

task-handoff.note: Handoff composition; assignment, permission, and persistence remain consumer-owned.

command-shortcuts.note: Command discovery composition; command execution remains consumer-owned.

dragDrop.rule: Drag/drop is an optional renderer affordance and is never the only path for a task-critical reorder or stage change.
dragDrop.keyboardAlternative: Every task-critical move has an explicit focusable action such as Move to lane, Move before, or Move after.

responsive.desktop: Use bounded collections, explicit workspaces, readable lanes, and visible action/status regions according to task focus.
responsive.tablet: Preserve primary identity, evidence, controls, and next action; move secondary context before shrinking below useful measure.
responsive.mobile: Use list/detail, lane selector/list, single-step, sheet, and safe-area patterns instead of compressing desktop compositions.
responsive.native: Native renderers consume the same semantic intent and states through platform-appropriate lists, stacks, sheets, and navigation.

accessibility: Every workflow region has an accessible name and a meaningful structure order.
Selection, current stage, status, progress, unread, and decision result are text-readable and never color-only.
Focus returns from drawers, sheets, and command surfaces; native alternatives preserve press, back, and safe-area feedback.
Keyboard and assistive technology users have explicit alternatives to drag, hover, and motion.
Loading, empty, error, disabled, read-only, stale, and pending-sync states remain distinguishable where the pattern needs them.

themeStudio.compatibility: All workflow patterns resolve through the same Ten4SevenProvider theme axes, density, contrast, and reduced-motion preferences exercised by Theme Studio.
themeStudio.noLocalPalette: Workflow compositions do not introduce feature-local colors, radii, shadows, control heights, or motion durations.

aiMetadata.retrieval: Retrieve this typed plane before selecting a workflow pattern; use implemented canonical components and linked recipes/blocks rather than inventing a domain primitive.
aiMetadata.compositionGuidance: Choose WorkQueue for operational records, Inbox for attention work, NotificationCenter for informational history, LifecycleTracker for one bounded lifecycle, Wizard for sequential steps, and Kanban/Workboard only when lanes add value.

compatibility: The typed U09 plane is the only workflow/productivity decision source; generated/workflow-productivity.json and packages/agent/generated/workflow-productivity.json are derived projections.
Existing operational recipes remain compatibility surfaces and are linked here; their business semantics do not migrate into generic components.
CommandPalette remains the alias of CommandMenu. New code should use CommandMenu; the alias does not increase canonical component count.
Timeline remains the existing ActivityFeed alias/intent. ActivityFeed is not CommentThread, NotificationCenter, or a durable audit store.
TaskBoard is a Kanban-oriented variant and Workboard is a block composition; neither creates a parallel primitive family.
Priority, urgency, SLA, assignment, escalation, and unread vocabularies remain consumer-owned mappings; no universal business enum is introduced.
Web CSS variables, native JS/TS values, AI metadata, and documentation are projections of the typed contract and never competing authorities.
U09 adds no DnD, workflow, comments, scheduler, editor, or native UI engine dependency.
deferred: Advanced DnD, touch gestures, keyboard reorder engine, collision strategy, and virtualization coordination are deferred to U10 after the move-intent seam is consumed.
CommentThread remains deferred until authoring, moderation, mention, sync, conflict, and persistence contracts are approved.
Domain workflow engines, approval policy, assignment/SLA/escalation systems, notification delivery, and audit stores remain consumer/domain work.
Additional native components are not created in U09; native canaries remain descriptors for a future renderer.
